statements.text: What do you think about the dangers and risks of the government potentially funding and moving toward algorithms that use AI technology to censor Americans online?
statements.context: Senate hearing on Artificial Intelligence in Government, Senator Scott posing a question to a witness.

statements.text: Snapchat admitted that their AI technology [...] is experimental, so do you agree that it is alarming and problematic that Snapchat would force their users, which comprise almost 60 percent of American teens, to use their chatbot features unless they paid to disable it with a subscription service? [...] If you do not want it, you have to pay to get it off, if you want to keep using Snapchat.
statements.context: Senate hearing on Artificial Intelligence in Government, questioning a witness about Snapchat's AI chatbot rollout.

statements.text: Artificial intelligence surely has productive uses, but it can also present great threats, especially to our children. [...] Today I am introducing my AI Shield for Kids (ASK) Act, to prevent children from accessing artificial intelligence features on social media sites without the consent of a parent or guardian.
statements.context: Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee hearing on AI in government, May 16, 2023.

statements.text: The CFPB has been leading a number of efforts on artificial intelligence, and we're working to bring on more technical talent inside the agency. We're taking steps to guard against algorithmic bias across credit markets, and we're working to ensure that data brokers respect longstanding laws on the books.
statements.context: Written responses by CFPB Director Rohit Chopra to questions from Chair Brown following the CFPB's Semiannual Report to Congress.

statements.text: Despite it being labeled a rule on artificial intelligence, your power grab to regulate emerging and existing technologies—even Excel spreadsheets—is beyond the SEC's scope and will ultimately stifle innovation.
statements.context: Senate Banking Committee oversight hearing on the SEC, with Ranking Member Scott delivering an opening statement criticizing Chair Gensler's regulatory agenda.

statements.text: But it also poses risks. Algorithms can replicate and even accelerate bias. Data points such as graduation dates or years of experience can serve as proxies for age, leading to older applicants being screened out automatically. Policymakers must ensure AI is used to expand opportunity, not entrench age discrimination, by supporting upskilling programs and enforcing protections against algorithmic bias.
statements.context: Opening statement by Chairman Scott at a U.S. Senate Special Committee on Aging hearing on protecting older workers.
